entries.answer:
Most már elegendő információm van a teljes rendszer minden részletéről. Megírom az átfogó, egyértelű, production-ready promptot Nim backendel és egyetlen `index.html`-es frontenddel.

***

## Átfogó rendszerépítési prompt

Az alábbi prompt a feltöltött dokumentáció alapján lett megírva. A leírás az eredeti szoftver neve nélkül, teljesen technikai, objektív és utasítás-fókuszált formában van megadva.[1]

***

```
Build a complete, production-ready, full-stack autonomous AI agent platform. The backend must be implemented entirely in a single Nim source file. The frontend must be implemented entirely in a single index.html file that includes all subpages, all JavaScript, and all CSS inline — no external files, no build steps, no placeholder content. Every feature described below must be fully implemented with real, working, unabridged code. No mock data, no simulated logic, no stubs, no TODO comments, no simplified versions.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PART 1 — BACKEND (single Nim file: server.nim)
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Use the `httpbeast` or `asynchttpserver` Nim library for the HTTP server. Use `std/asyncdispatch`, `std/json`, `std/strutils`, `std/tables`, `std/times`, `std/os`, `std/osproc`, `std/base64`, `std/sha1` (or equivalent hashing), and `std/uri`. Use SQLite via the `db_sqlite` standard library for all persistent storage. Use `std/httpclient` for outbound HTTP calls to external AI APIs and third-party services.

The server must listen on port 8080 and serve all API routes under `/api/` and the static frontend under `/`.

1.1 DATABASE SCHEMA

Create the following SQLite tables on startup if they do not exist:

  users(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, plan TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free', credits INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 100, timezone TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC', created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  sessions(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), token TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  projects(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, owner_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), name TEXT NOT NULL, master_instruction TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, pinned INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, sort_order INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)

  project_members(project_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id), user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), joined_at INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(project_id, user_id))

  project_files(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, project_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id), filename TEXT NOT NULL, content BLOB NOT NULL, mime_type TEXT NOT NULL, uploaded_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  tasks(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, project_id TEXT, owner_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), title TEXT NOT NULL, prompt TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', mode TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'agent', agent_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'general', output TEXT, output_format TEXT, scheduled_at INTEGER, recurrence TEXT, last_run_at INTEGER, credits_used INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, favorited INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)

  task_steps(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id), step_index INTEGER NOT NULL, tool_name TEXT NOT NULL, tool_input TEXT NOT NULL, tool_output TEXT, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', started_at INTEGER, finished_at INTEGER)

  task_collaborators(task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id), user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), invited_by TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), joined_at INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(task_id, user_id))

  task_files(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id), filename TEXT NOT NULL, content BLOB NOT NULL, mime_type TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  messages(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id), user_id TEXT, role TEXT NOT NULL, content TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  wide_research_jobs(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id), total_items INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_items INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running', created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  wide_research_sub_tasks(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, job_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES wide_research_jobs(id), item_index INTEGER NOT NULL, item_prompt TEXT NOT NULL, result TEXT, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', started_at INTEGER, finished_at INTEGER)

  skills(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, owner_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), name TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL, skill_md TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user', created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  integrations(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), type TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, config TEXT NOT NULL, access_token TEXT, refresh_token TEXT, expires_at INTEGER, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  mcp_servers(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), name TEXT NOT NULL, url TEXT NOT NULL, auth_type TEXT NOT NULL, auth_value TEXT, tools_json TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  scheduled_tasks(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id), cron_expression TEXT NOT NULL, next_run_at INTEGER NOT NULL, enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  notifications(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), title TEXT NOT NULL, body TEXT NOT NULL, read INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  websites(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id), owner_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), name TEXT NOT NULL, subdomain TEXT UNIQUE, custom_domain TEXT, ssl_enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, published INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, html TEXT NOT NULL, backend_code TEXT, db_schema TEXT, env_vars TEXT, seo_enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, seo_title TEXT, seo_description TEXT, seo_keywords TEXT, analytics_enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  website_analytics(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, website_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES websites(id), event_type TEXT NOT NULL, path TEXT NOT NULL, referrer TEXT, user_agent TEXT, ip_hash TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  website_users(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, website_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES websites(id), email TEXT NOT NULL, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user', created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  mail_workflows(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), name TEXT NOT NULL, bot_address TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, default_prompt TEXT NOT NULL, filter_from TEXT, filter_subject TEXT, enabled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  mail_messages(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, workflow_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES mail_workflows(id), from_address TEXT NOT NULL, subject TEXT NOT NULL, body TEXT NOT NULL, attachments TEXT, processed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, result_task_id TEXT, received_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  credit_transactions(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), amount INTEGER NOT NULL, reason TEXT NOT NULL, task_id TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  data_sources(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, type TEXT NOT NULL, base_url TEXT NOT NULL, auth_header TEXT, description TEXT NOT NULL)

  browser_sessions(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id), user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), session_type TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending', authorized INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, log TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

  design_projects(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id), owner_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id), base_image BLOB, current_image BLOB, edit_history TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

1.2 AUTHENTICATION

Implement JWT-like token authentication using HMAC-SHA256. All tokens are stored in the `sessions` table. Token expiry is 30 days. 

Endpoints:
  POST /api/auth/register  — body: {email, password}; creates user with hashed password (bcrypt-like using SHA-256 + salt), returns {token, user}
  POST /api/auth/login     — body: {email, password}; validates credentials, returns {token, user}
  POST /api/auth/logout    — invalidates session token
  GET  /api/auth/me        — returns current authenticated user object

All endpoints except register and login require the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. A middleware function must validate the token and attach the user to the request context before calling the handler.

1.3 USER MANAGEMENT

  GET    /api/users/me                — full user profile
  PUT    /api/users/me                — update email, timezone, notification preferences
  PUT    /api/users/me/password       — change password
  GET    /api/users/me/credits        — current credit balance and transaction history
  GET    /api/users/me/notifications  — paginated list of notifications
  PUT    /api/users/me/notifications/:id/read — mark notification as read
  DELETE /api/users/me/notifications/:id

1.4 PROJECTS

  GET    /api/projects              — list all projects for authenticated user (with member info, task count)
  POST   /api/projects              — create project {name, master_instruction}
  GET    /api/projects/:id          — get project detail
  PUT    /api/projects/:id          — update project {name, master_instruction, pinned, sort_order}
  DELETE /api/projects/:id          — delete project and all associated tasks
  POST   /api/projects/:id/members  — invite user by email {email}
  DELETE /api/projects/:id/members/:user_id — remove member
  GET    /api/projects/:id/files    — list project knowledge base files
  POST   /api/projects/:id/files    — upload file (multipart/form-data)
  DELETE /api/projects/:id/files/:file_id — delete file
  PUT    /api/projects/reorder      — body: [{id, sort_order}] — bulk reorder projects

1.5 TASKS

  GET    /api/tasks                    — list tasks (query params: project_id, filter=[all|non_project|favorites|scheduled], page, limit)
  POST   /api/tasks                    — create task {title, prompt, project_id?, mode, agent_type, output_format?, scheduled_at?, recurrence?}
  GET    /api/tasks/:id                — get task with all steps, messages, files, collaborators
  PUT    /api/tasks/:id                — update task {title, favorited, project_id}
  DELETE /api/tasks/:id                — delete task and all associated data
  POST   /api/tasks/:id/run            — trigger async execution of the task
  POST   /api/tasks/:id/stop           — stop running task
  GET    /api/tasks/:id/messages       — paginated message history
  POST   /api/tasks/:id/messages       — send a new message into the task context and re-run
  GET    /api/tasks/:id/files          — list output files
  GET    /api/tasks/:id/files/:file_id — download a file
  POST   /api/tasks/:id/collaborators  — invite collaborator {email}
  DELETE /api/tasks/:id/collaborators/:user_id
  GET    /api/tasks/:id/steps          — list all agent execution steps

The task execution engine (run endpoint) must:
  1. Load the task, its project's master_instruction, the project's knowledge base files, the user's connected integrations, and any active skills mentioned in the prompt (via slash-command prefix detection).
  2. Construct a system prompt by combining: master_instruction + skill contents (if any) + uploaded file summaries.
  3. Call an external LLM API (configurable via OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variables) using the full messages history as context.
  4. Parse the LLM response for tool calls. Supported tools: web_search(query), fetch_url(url), run_code(language, code), read_file(file_id), write_file(filename, content, mime_type), call_integration(integration_id, method, params), call_mcp_server(server_id, tool_name, params), image_generate(prompt, model), image_understand(image_base64, question), speech_to_text(audio_base64), text_to_speech(text, voice), video_understand(url, question), wide_research_dispatch(items[], item_prompt_template), browser_open(url, session_type), browser_action(session_id, action, params).
  5. Execute each tool call, record the step in `task_steps`, append the result to the message context.
  6. Loop until the LLM emits a final answer or the step count exceeds 50.
  7. Persist the final output to `tasks.output`, set status to 'completed', deduct credits from user balance, record credit transaction.

Tool implementations:
  - web_search: call a configurable search API (SERP_API_KEY env var) and return top 5 results as JSON.
  - fetch_url: use std/httpclient to GET the URL, strip HTML tags, return first 8000 chars.
  - run_code: use std/osproc to execute Python3 code in a temp directory with a 30-second timeout; capture stdout/stderr.
  - read_file: load file content from task_files or project_files by ID.
  - write_file: insert into task_files, return file_id.
  - call_integration: look up the integration by ID and user, dispatch to the correct integration handler (see section 1.10).
  - call_mcp_server: make an HTTP POST to the MCP server URL with the tool call JSON, return the response.
  - image_generate: call the image generation API (IMAGE_API_KEY env var, model parameter selects standard or high-quality), return base64 PNG.
  - image_understand: call the vision API with base64 image, return text description.
  - speech_to_text: call the speech API (SPEECH_API_KEY env var), return transcription.
  - text_to_speech: call the TTS API, return base64 audio MP3.
  - video_understand: fetch video, call video understanding API, return text.
  - wide_research_dispatch: create a wide_research_job record, spawn N sub-tasks by inserting into wide_research_sub_tasks, then execute each in parallel using asyncdispatch futures, collect results, synthesize.
  - browser_open: insert a browser_sessions record, return session_id. If session_type is 'local', mark as waiting for user authorization. If 'cloud', mark as authorized and simulate browser actions via headless browser commands through osproc (using chromium-browser --headless if available).
  - browser_action: execute a browser action (navigate, click, type, extract_text, screenshot) in the given session.

1.6 WIDE RESEARCH

  POST /api/wide-research         — create a new wide research job {task_id, items[], item_prompt_template}
  GET  /api/wide-research/:job_id — get job status, completed/total count, and all sub-task results

1.7 SCHEDULED TASKS

A background goroutine-equivalent using `asyncdispatch` must poll every 60 seconds for scheduled tasks where `next_run_at <= now()` and `enabled = 1`. For each due task, execute the task (same as POST /api/tasks/:id/run), then compute the next run time from the cron expression and update `next_run_at`.

  GET    /api/scheduled           — list all scheduled tasks for current user
  POST   /api/scheduled           — create scheduled task {task_id, cron_expression}
  PUT    /api/scheduled/:id       — update {cron_expression, enabled}
  DELETE /api/scheduled/:id       — delete scheduled task

1.8 SKILLS

  GET    /api/skills              — list all skills for current user (metadata only: id, name, description)
  POST   /api/skills              — create skill {name, description, skill_md, source}
  GET    /api/skills/:id          — get full skill including skill_md content
  PUT    /api/skills/:id          — update skill
  DELETE /api/skills/:id          — delete skill
  POST   /api/skills/import-github — body: {repo_url}; fetch the repository's SKILL.md via GitHub raw content API, parse name/description from frontmatter, create skill record

1.9 INTEGRATIONS (MCP Connectors)

  GET    /api/integrations             — list all integrations for user
  POST   /api/integrations             — create integration {type, name, config, access_token?, refresh_token?, expires_at?}
  DELETE /api/integrations/:id         — disconnect integration
  GET    /api/integrations/available   — return list of supported integration types with descriptions

The supported integration types and their dispatch logic in call_integration:
  gmail:           use access_token to call Gmail REST API v1 (search messages, get message, send message, list threads)
  google_calendar: use access_token to call Google Calendar API v3 (list events, create event, update event, delete event)
  google_drive:    use access_token to call Google Drive API v3 (list files, download file, upload file, create folder)
  notion:          use access_token to call Notion API v1 (search, get page, create page, update page, query database)
  slack:           use access_token to call Slack Web API (post message, list channels, get thread messages)
  hubspot:         use access_token to call HubSpot CRM API v3 (get contacts, create contact, update deal)
  stripe:          use auth_value (secret key) to call Stripe API v1 (list charges, get balance, list invoices, create payment link)
  github:          use access_token to call GitHub REST API v3 (list repos, create issue, list pull requests, list commits, create file)
  hugging_face:    use auth_value (API token) to call Hugging Face Inference API (run model inference)
  zapier:          use auth_value (webhook URL) to POST a payload to a Zapier webhook

Each integration dispatch function must construct the correct HTTP request (headers, body) and return parsed JSON. All tokens must be stored encrypted at rest using XOR with a server-side secret (SERVER_SECRET env var).

1.10 MCP SERVERS (Custom)

  GET    /api/mcp-servers          — list user's custom MCP servers
  POST   /api/mcp-servers          — add server {name, url, auth_type, auth_value}; fetch tools list from url/tools
  PUT    /api/mcp-servers/:id      — update server
  DELETE /api/mcp-servers/:id      — delete server

When a custom MCP server is called via the tool engine, the backend sends:
  POST {server_url}/call
  Body: {"tool": "<tool_name>", "params": {<params_json>}}
  Headers: Authorization based on auth_type (Bearer, ApiKey, or None)
  Returns the JSON response body to the agent.

1.11 MAIL WORKFLOWS

  GET    /api/mail-workflows           — list all mail workflows
  POST   /api/mail-workflows           — create {name, default_prompt, filter_from?, filter_subject?}; auto-generate a unique bot_address
  PUT    /api/mail-workflows/:id       — update workflow settings
  DELETE /api/mail-workflows/:id       — delete workflow

  POST   /api/mail/inbound             — receive an inbound email webhook (from email service provider); body: {to, from, subject, body_text, attachments[]}; match to workflow by `to` address; verify sender against filter rules; create a task with the default_prompt + email body as context; return 200

  GET    /api/mail-workflows/:id/messages — list processed messages

1.12 WEBSITES (Web App Builder)

  GET    /api/websites             — list all websites owned by user
  POST   /api/websites             — create website {name, task_id} (task output becomes initial HTML)
  GET    /api/websites/:id         — get website details
  PUT    /api/websites/:id         — update {name, html, backend_code, db_schema, env_vars, seo_enabled, seo_title, seo_description, seo_keywords, analytics_enabled}
  DELETE /api/websites/:id         — delete website
  POST   /api/websites/:id/publish — set published=1, auto-assign subdomain if none set
  POST   /api/websites/:id/unpublish
  POST   /api/websites/:id/custom-domain — body: {domain}; update custom_domain, return required DNS records (A record and CNAME)
  GET    /api/websites/:id/analytics — return aggregated analytics (page views per day, top pages, top referrers, device breakdown from user-agent)
  POST   /api/websites/:id/analytics/event — record a page view event {path, referrer, user_agent}
  GET    /api/websites/:id/users   — list registered website users
  POST   /api/websites/:id/users   — create website user {email, password, role}
  DELETE /api/websites/:id/users/:user_id

Serving published websites: when a request comes in with Host header matching a known subdomain (*.localhost or configured domain), look up the website by subdomain or custom_domain, serve the `html` field as HTML. Inject analytics tracking script before </body>. Serve the backend_code by executing it server-side (if non-empty) as a sandboxed Nim eval or Python subprocess.

  POST /api/websites/:id/seo/optimize — analyze the website HTML, generate seo_title, seo_description, seo_keywords using the LLM, update the record, return the new values

1.13 DESIGN PROJECTS

  POST /api/design                 — create design project {task_id, base_image_base64}
  GET  /api/design/:id             — get current design state and edit history
  POST /api/design/:id/edit        — apply an edit {selections: [{x,y,w,h, instruction}], reference_image_base64?}
                                     call image editing API with the mask and instruction, update current_image, append to edit_history
  POST /api/design/:id/edit-text   — extract text regions from current_image using vision API, return list of {id, text, bounding_box}
  PUT  /api/design/:id/text/:text_id — update a text region: inpaint using image API with new text

1.14 COLLABORATION (Real-Time)

Implement Server-Sent Events (SSE) for real-time updates:

  GET /api/tasks/:id/events — SSE stream; the server pushes events when:
    - a new step is added to the task
    - a new message is added
    - a collaborator sends a prompt
    - task status changes
  
  GET /api/projects/:id/events — SSE stream for project-level updates

SSE event format: `data: <json_payload>\n\n`

Maintain an in-memory table (Table[string, seq[AsyncHttpResponse]]) mapping task_id to connected SSE clients. On every database write to task_steps or messages, iterate the client list and push the event.

1.15 BROWSER SESSIONS

  GET  /api/browser-sessions/:id         — get session status and log
  POST /api/browser-sessions/:id/authorize — user authorizes a pending local browser session
  POST /api/browser-sessions/:id/takeover  — user requests to take over the browser from the agent
  POST /api/browser-sessions/:id/return    — user returns control to the agent after takeover
  GET  /api/browser-sessions/:id/events    — SSE stream of browser action log entries

1.16 DATA SOURCES

On startup, pre-populate the `data_sources` table with the following entries if it is empty:
  {name: "Market Research", type: "social_company_financial", base_url: "", description: "Competitive intelligence from social media, company profiles, and financial data"}
  {name: "Investment Analysis", type: "stock_sec_market", base_url: "", description: "Stock performance, SEC filings, and market insights"}
  {name: "Content Discovery", type: "video_social", base_url: "", description: "Trending content analysis across video platforms"}
  {name: "Economic Research", type: "macro_economic", base_url: "", description: "Global economic indicators and macroeconomic data"}

  GET /api/data-sources — list available data sources

The LLM tool engine must detect when a prompt mentions any data source name or type and automatically include a call_data_source(source_id, query) tool invocation in the planning phase.

1.17 SLACK INTEGRATION (Webhook)

  POST /api/slack/events — receive Slack event webhook; verify signature using SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET env var; handle app_mention events by extracting the thread ts, channel, and text; look up or create a task for that thread; run the task; post the result back to the Slack thread via Slack Web API chat.postMessage.

1.18 NANO BANANA PRO (Image Generation Model)

The image_generate tool supports a `model` parameter. When model is "nano_banana_pro", call the high-quality image generation endpoint (NANO_BANANA_API_KEY env var). This model must support:
  - Generating images with legible embedded text
  - Batch generation (up to 12 slides) from a single prompt with slide_count and style parameters
  - Reference image input for style matching

  POST /api/image/generate — body: {prompt, model, width?, height?, slide_count?, style?, reference_image_base64?}; returns {images: [base64_png, ...]}
  POST /api/image/understand — body: {image_base64, question}; returns {answer: string}

1.19 SLIDES ENGINE

  POST /api/slides                — create a slides job {prompt, template_pptx_base64?, theme?, slide_count?, audience?, goal?, use_wide_research?}
  GET  /api/slides/:id            — get slide job status and output
  GET  /api/slides/:id/download   — download the generated .pptx file (base64-encoded PPTX structure built by writing an OpenXML ZIP file in Nim using std/zip or constructing raw XML strings)

The slides engine must:
  1. Accept the prompt and options.
  2. Optionally run web research if use_wide_research is true.
  3. Use the LLM to generate a structured JSON outline: {title, slides: [{title, content_points[], speaker_notes, image_prompt, chart_data?}]}.
  4. For each slide, call image_generate if an image_prompt is present.
  5. Assemble a valid .pptx (OpenXML) file in memory by constructing the required XML files (presentation.xml, slide1.xml ... slideN.xml, slideLayout, slideMaster, [Content_Types].xml, _rels/.rels) and writing them as a ZIP.
  6. Store the binary ZIP in task_files, return the file_id.
  7. Also render an HTML slide viewer (all slides as div elements with CSS transitions) and store in task output.

1.20 DATA ANALYSIS ENGINE

  POST /api/analysis              — create an analysis job {task_id, data_file_id, request_text, chart_types[], output_format}
  GET  /api/analysis/:id          — get status and output

The analysis engine must:
  1. Load the data file (CSV or XLSX) from task_files.
  2. Parse CSV using std/parsecsv. For XLSX, convert to CSV using a Python subprocess call.
  3. Call the LLM with the CSV contents and analysis request to produce: {summary, insights[], charts: [{type, title, labels[], datasets[]}]}.
  4. For each chart, generate a Chart.js-compatible JSON config.
  5. Assemble the output as a self-contained HTML page with Chart.js CDN, or a Markdown report, or a JSON dataset, based on output_format.
  6. Store the output in task_files.

1.21 CREDIT SYSTEM

Credit deduction rules (deduct from user.credits after each task step):
  - LLM call (per 1000 tokens): 1 credit
  - Image generation: 5 credits
  - Wide research sub-task: 2 credits each
  - Slides generation: 10 credits per deck
  - Speech/TTS call: 2 credits
  - Web search: 1 credit per search

Before running any task, estimate the credit cost and reject with HTTP 402 if the user has insufficient credits.

  POST /api/credits/topup — body: {amount}; create a credit_transaction record (in production, this would link to a Stripe payment)

1.22 WEBSITE PAYMENTS (Stripe Integration for Builder)

  POST /api/websites/:id/payments/setup — create a Stripe sandbox/live configuration for the website; stores product IDs and webhook secret in website.env_vars; returns checkout session URL for testing

  POST /api/websites/:id/payments/go-live — transition from sandbox to live Stripe keys; requires the user to provide their own Stripe secret key {stripe_secret_key}

1.23 ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES

The server reads all secrets from environment variables:
  OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, IMAGE_API_KEY, NANO_BANANA_API_KEY, SPEECH_API_KEY, SERP_API_KEY, SERVER_SECRET, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, DATABASE_PATH (default: ./data.db), PORT (default: 8080)

1.24 ERROR HANDLING AND LOGGING

Every HTTP handler must catch exceptions with try/except and return structured JSON errors:
  {"error": {"code": "<error_code>", "message": "<human_readable>"}}
with appropriate HTTP status codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 429, 500).

Log all requests to stdout: `[<timestamp>] <method> <path> <status> <duration_ms>ms`
Log all tool calls: `[TOOL] task=<id> tool=<name> status=<ok|error> duration=<ms>ms`

All subpages/views are implemented as JavaScript-driven single-page application (SPA) using a client-side router that reads `window.location.hash`.

2.24 API COMMUNICATION LAYER

Implement a single `api(method, path, body)` async function in JavaScript that:
  - Reads the token from localStorage.
  - Sets Authorization header.
  - Sets Content-Type: application/json.
  - On 401, clears token and redirects to #/login.
  - On error, extracts error.message from the JSON response body and shows a toast.
  - Returns the parsed JSON response body on success.

Also implement a `sseConnect(path, handlers)` function that creates an EventSource, registers onmessage and onerror handlers, and returns the EventSource object (so callers can close it on view unmount).

3.1 The Nim backend file must compile with: `nim c -d:ssl -d:release -o:server server.nim`

3.2 The frontend index.html must be served by the Nim backend at the root route `GET /`. Any path not starting with `/api/` must return the index.html contents.

3.3 Provide a README.md (separate from the two main files) that documents:
  - All required environment variables and their purpose
  - How to compile and run
  - How to run tests (describe what manual tests verify each major endpoint)
  - Database schema overview

3.4 The backend must handle CORS: respond to OPTIONS preflight requests with Allow-Origin: *, Allow-Methods: GET,POST,PUT,DELETE,OPTIONS, Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization.

3.5 Rate limiting: in-memory request counter per IP address; reject with HTTP 429 if more than 100 requests per minute from the same IP.

ABSOLUTE REQUIREMENTS SUMMARY
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

- The entire backend is in exactly one file: server.nim
- The entire frontend is in exactly one file: index.html (no separate JS/CSS/image files)
- All code is complete and production-ready — no TODOs, no placeholder functions, no commented-out sections, no "implement later" notes
- All database operations use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
- All user passwords are stored as salted SHA-256 hashes (minimum), never in plaintext
- All sensitive tokens in the integrations table are XOR-encrypted with SERVER_SECRET
- The SPA router handles the browser back button correctly (hashchange event listener)
- All views handle empty states (no tasks yet, no projects yet, etc.) with helpful empty state UI
- All forms validate inputs client-side before submission
- The UI is fully responsive down to 768px viewport width
- All async operations in the Nim backend use asyncdispatch; the server is never blocked by a synchronous operation longer than 1ms (long operations use async futures or spawn via osproc)
```
